title: Witness pair (S - A, A) for the Doob-Meyer decomposition of a cadlag class D submartingale
intent: Prove the Doob-Meyer decomposition -- every cadlag submartingale of class D is the sum of a cadlag martingale and a predictable, cadlag, monotone increasing process vanishing at bottom -- by constructing the two witnesses M := S - A and A := G.indicator L (the limsup of convex step extensions, restricted to a good set of full measure) and discharging each conjunct of the resulting existence statement from the martingale-part and predictable-part lemmas.

parent.name: ProbabilityTheory.ClassD.doob_meyer
parent.statement:
theorem ProbabilityTheory.ClassD.doob_meyer {ι Ω : Type*} [CompleteLinearOrder ι]
    [TopologicalSpace ι] [OrderTopology ι] [SecondCountableTopology ι] [MeasurableSpace ι]
    [BorelSpace ι] {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure P] {S : ι → Ω → ℝ}
    {𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ} [𝓕.IsRightContinuous] [𝓕.IsComplete P]
    (hd : ClassD S 𝓕 P) (hs : Submartingale S 𝓕 P) (hc : ∀ ω, IsCadlag (S · ω)) :
    ∃ (M A : ι → Ω → ℝ), S = M + A ∧ Martingale M 𝓕 P ∧ (∀ ω, IsCadlag (M · ω)) ∧
      IsStronglyPredictable 𝓕 A ∧ (∀ ω, IsCadlag (A · ω)) ∧ (∀ ω, Monotone (A · ω)) ∧
      A ⊥ = 0

children.name: isCadlag_martingalePartLim
children.statement:
lemma isCadlag_martingalePartLim (hd : ClassD S 𝓕 P) (hs : Submartingale S 𝓕 P) (ω : Ω) :
    IsCadlag (martingalePartLim hd hs · ω)
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The paths of the martingale part `martingalePartLim hd hs` are cadlag.

children.name: martingale_martingalePartLim
children.statement:
lemma martingale_martingalePartLim [𝓕.IsRightContinuous] [𝓕.IsComplete P]
    (hd : ClassD S 𝓕 P) (hs : Submartingale S 𝓕 P) :
    Martingale (martingalePartLim hd hs) 𝓕 P
children.closed_by: refine ⟨stronglyAdapted_martingalePartLim hd hs, fun i j hij ↦ ?_⟩; a calc of conditional expectations via condExp_congr_ae, condExp_ae_eq and martingalePartLim_ae_eq
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The martingale part `martingalePartLim hd hs` is a martingale under the usual conditions.

children.name: isCadlag_predictablePartLim_ae
children.statement:
lemma isCadlag_predictablePartLim_ae {ι Ω : Type*} [TopologicalSpace ι]
    [SecondCountableTopology ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [LinearOrder ι] [OrderBot ι] [OrderTop ι]
    [OrderTopology ι] {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsFiniteMeasure P] {S : ι → Ω → ℝ} {𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ} (hd : ClassD S 𝓕 P)
    (hs : Submartingale S 𝓕 P) (hc : ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, IsCadlag (S · ω)) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, IsCadlag (predictablePartLim hd hs · ω)
children.closed_by: filter_upwards [hc] with ω hω; exact hω.sub (isCadlag_martingalePartLim hd hs ω)
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If S is almost surely cadlag, so is the predictable part `predictablePartLim hd hs`.

children.name: predictablePartLim_monotone_ae
children.statement:
lemma predictablePartLim_monotone_ae {ι Ω : Type*} [TopologicalSpace ι]
    [SecondCountableTopology ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [LinearOrder ι] [OrderBot ι] [OrderTop ι]
    [OrderTopology ι] {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsFiniteMeasure P] {S : ι → Ω → ℝ} {𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ} [𝓕.IsRightContinuous]
    (hd : ClassD S 𝓕 P) (hs : Submartingale S 𝓕 P) (hc : ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, IsCadlag (S · ω)) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, Monotone fun t ↦ predictablePartLim hd hs t ω
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: If S is almost surely cadlag, the predictable part is almost surely monotone.

children.name: isStronglyPredictable_limsup_predictableConvexStep
children.statement:
lemma isStronglyPredictable_limsup_predictableConvexStep {ι Ω : Type*} [TopologicalSpace ι]
    [SecondCountableTopology ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [LinearOrder ι] [OrderBot ι]
    [OrderTop ι] [OrderTopology ι] {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsFiniteMeasure P] {S : ι → Ω → ℝ} {𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ} (hd : ClassD S 𝓕 P)
    (hs : Submartingale S 𝓕 P) :
    IsStronglyPredictable 𝓕 (fun t ω => limsup (predictableConvexStep hd hs · t ω) atTop)
children.closed_by: IsStronglyPredictable.limsup fun n => isStronglyPredictable_predictableConvexStep hd hs n
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The limsup of the convex step extensions of the predictable parts is strongly predictable.

children.name: predictableConvexStep_bot
children.statement:
lemma predictableConvexStep_bot (hd : ClassD S 𝓕 P) (hs : Submartingale S 𝓕 P) (n : ℕ) :
    predictableConvexStep hd hs n ⊥ = 0
children.closed_by: funext ω; simp [predictableConvexStep, Finsupp.sum, Finset.sum_apply, predictableSeqStep_bot]
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The convex step extension of the predictable parts vanishes at ⊥.

children.name: limsup_predictableConvexStep_eq_predictablePartLim
children.statement:
lemma limsup_predictableConvexStep_eq_predictablePartLim {ι : Type*} [CompleteLinearOrder ι]
    [TopologicalSpace ι] [OrderTopology ι] [SecondCountableTopology ι] [MeasurableSpace ι]
    [BorelSpace ι] {S : ι → Ω → ℝ} {𝓕 : Filtration ι mΩ} [𝓕.IsRightContinuous] [𝓕.IsComplete P]
    (hd : ClassD S 𝓕 P) (hs : Submartingale S 𝓕 P) (hc : ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, IsCadlag (S · ω)) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, ∀ t, limsup (predictableConvexStep hd hs · t ω) atTop =
      predictablePartLim hd hs t ω
children.closed_by: le_antisymm; a début-time contradiction: debut_mem_set_of_finite puts the début in B k while L and A coincide there
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The limsup process and `predictablePartLim hd hs` are indistinguishable.

children.name: measurableSet_predictable_univ_prod
children.statement:
lemma measurableSet_predictable_univ_prod {s : Set Ω} (hs : MeasurableSet[𝓕 ⊥] s) :
    MeasurableSet[𝓕.predictable] (univ ×ˢ s)
children.closed_by: rw [univ = {⊥} ∪ Ioi ⊥, union_prod]; MeasurableSet.union with measurableSet_predictable_singleton_bot_prod and measurableSet_predictable_Ioi_prod
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The set `univ ×ˢ s` is predictable for an 𝓕⊥-measurable set s.

applicability.goal_shape: An existence goal `∃ (M A : ι → Ω → ℝ), S = M + A ∧ …` whose witnesses are processes assembled from earlier definitions (the martingale part `martingalePartLim`, the predictable part `predictablePartLim`, the limsup of convex step extensions); the body is a conjunction of measurability, pointwise and path-regularity properties of the witnesses.
applicability.use_when: the witnesses factor through objects whose properties are already proved in separate lemmas (here the martingale-part and predictable-part lemmas), so each conjunct of the existence statement is discharged by one lemma and the glue only splices them onto the chosen witnesses.
applicability.avoid_when: the witnesses are not canonical or their properties are not already lemmatised (each conjunct would then need a fresh argument in the glue, and the witnesses chosen for one conjunct may not satisfy the next); or the existence statement is too weak to pin down a witness.

consequences: The move turns one existence goal into one obligation per conjunct of the body, each discharged against a witness. The witnesses M := S - A and A := G.indicator L must be chosen so that every conjunct is a lemma already proved about that object: the martingale property comes from `martingale_martingalePartLim`, path regularity of A from the definition of the good set G (whose complement is null via `limsup_predictableConvexStep_eq_predictablePartLim`, `predictablePartLim_monotone_ae`, `isCadlag_predictablePartLim_ae`), and A ⊥ = 0 from `predictableConvexStep_bot`. Failure modes: picking a witness that satisfies some conjuncts but not others (e.g. a predictable part that is not monotone off the good set), or a good set that is not full measure, which forces the off-set branches (the `by_cases hω : ω ∈ G` cases) to prove the properties from scratch for the constant 0 process.
